frozen_definitions.base_datum: D consists only of the unoriented raw graph, the full automorphism action, and the characteristic Z1 < Z2 tower.
frozen_definitions.canonical_selector: A selector constructed from D must be invariant under every isomorphism or automorphism preserving D.
frozen_definitions.evolver_candidate: An exactly defined admissible action H on an explicitly declared lifted carrier. No candidate may be introduced after its orientation behavior has been inspected.
frozen_definitions.exchange_symmetry: A D-preserving symmetry sigma exchanges H and inverse(H).
frozen_definitions.reversal: The reversal involution sends an evolver H to inverse(H).
frozen_definitions.self_inverse: H is self-inverse exactly when H equals inverse(H).

frozen_native_outcomes.computation_failure: The candidate action, inverse, carrier, or symmetry action cannot be reconstructed consistently.
frozen_native_outcomes.exact_reversal_obstruction: A preregistered non-self-inverse evolver pair exists, a D-preserving symmetry exchanges its members, and no D-invariant singleton selector exists.
frozen_native_outcomes.multiple_reversal_orbits: The base datum preserves more than one admissible unordered pair, so even the pair is not canonically selected.
frozen_native_outcomes.no_exact_evolver_candidate: No exact, preregistered evolver candidate can be constructed from the available algebraic authorities.
frozen_native_outcomes.self_inverse_collapse: The admitted candidate satisfies H equals inverse(H), so there is no distinct orientation pair for this candidate.
frozen_native_outcomes.unique_orientation_selected: The base datum D intrinsically distinguishes one orientation and the proposed exchange symmetry does not preserve D.

general_obstruction_theorem.conclusion: No canonical selector from D can select exactly one member of the pair {H, inverse(H)}.
hypotheses: H is an admitted evolver candidate defined before orientation testing.
H is not equal to inverse(H).
There exists a symmetry sigma preserving D.
Sigma sends H to inverse(H) and inverse(H) to H.
A canonical selector from D is invariant under sigma.
proof_scheme: Assume a canonical selector from D chooses H.
Invariance requires the selected output to remain H.
The exchange property requires the selected output to become inverse(H).
Therefore H equals inverse(H), contradicting the distinctness hypothesis.

minimal_additional_datum_standard.necessary_condition: The stabilizer of the additional datum must exclude every D-preserving symmetry that exchanges H and inverse(H).
minimal_additional_datum_standard.sufficiency_condition: After adjoining the datum, exactly one member of the reversal pair is selected.
